# Supplementary Table 5. The nine levers and their levels, with values (generated by tools/pathways_methods.py; do not edit; main-paper Table 1 is LEVERS_TABLE_MAIN.md)

Ambition levels follow the 2050 Pathways Calculator (DECC 2010; DESNZ 2023) and EUCalc (Kockat et al. 2019, Table 2): Reference = Level 1, Moderate = Level 2, Ambitious = Level 3, theoretical limit (TL) = Level 4. One rule for every lever (the 'rule' column): the Reference is current practice held (2023 / 2025 values; business-as-usual technology change applies in every run); Moderate is the midpoint of the Reference and Ambitious (exact for every lever); Ambitious is a documented frontier, achieved somewhere or projected by an authority, and cited; the theoretical limit is the logical bound where the lever has one (zero vacancy, zero space beyond the occupied area, no demolition, 100% brownfield, zero A4-A5), otherwise the best value observed (TL1 household size; the lowest-carbon NZ case study for materials). TL A4-A5 = 0 is a theoretical bound: construction waste cannot strictly reach zero, and LCAQuick does not split A4 from A5. Ambitious takes the first applicable sub-rule: A, a case-study distribution exists: the Harrell-Davis q0.15 quantile of the pooled scale-free case ratios (the top-15% convention of the EU Taxonomy, Delegated Regulation 2021/2139, Annex I s. 7.7), with a percentile bootstrap interval; B, an NZ record with no structural trend exists: the best value ever observed in NZ; C, otherwise: a published reference value (official projection > legislated target > peer-reviewed scenario > peer-country value). Moderate is the exact midpoint between the Reference and Ambitious in the lever's native parameter (per year for the path levers L1 and L9). TL is the definitional zero or full where one exists, else the best single observation, and is asserted at least as strong as Ambitious. Every level moves from the Reference along the normalised logistic 2026 -> 2035 (midpoint 2030.5, k = ln(81)/6), with two documented exceptions: L9 Ambitious and Moderate follow their own path (linear from the 2026 Reference value to zero in 2050, which is the phase-in itself); TL1 rises at the fastest observed inter-census change of household size (the behavioural speed limit) and reaches its level after 2035.
